Q: Error "variable is not defined", but the variable can be called in the console A:

I thick I had the same issue.

I'm using Python 3.10 with Spyder. The variable was visible in the console and in the Variable Explorer, but when I ran the script it raised: name 'I' is not defined.

The problem was that Spyder was running the file in an empty namespace, not in the console’s namespace.

I fixed it by going to:

Tools → Preferences → Run

and activating:

  • Execute in current console

  • Run in console’s namespace instead of an empty one

  • The directory of the file being executed

After that the variable is recognized correctly.

Q: Why are there different results in evaluating e sequence of forms in emacs elisp? A:

The reason is Lexical vs Dynamic binding.

C-hf eval-buffer tells us:

This function ignores the current value of the ‘lexical-binding’ variable. Instead it will heed any
-*- lexical-binding: t -*-
settings in the buffer, and if there is no such setting, the buffer will be evaluated without lexical binding.

So when you use that in the *scratch* buffer (which does not include that comment in its default contents), my/stream-enumerate-interval is defined using dynamic binding.

The macro call within the function definition results in another function (lambda () (my/stream-enumerate-interval (1+ l) h)) which ends up being called in my/sicp-force outside of the scope of any dynamically-bound l; hence (under dynamic binding) Lisp error: (void-variable l).

However, the *scratch* buffer does (nowadays) set lexical-binding buffer-locally, and consequently when you explicitly eval the my/stream-enumerate-interval definition with eval-defun or eval-last-sexp, you're doing so under lexical binding.

Under lexical binding, that function definition (from the expanded macro call) is defined with a lexical environment including l, and so it works as you expected.

If you add the -*- lexical-binding: t -*- comment, then eval-buffer will respect it. You can use M-x add-file-local-variable-prop-line RET lexical-binding RET t RET

I think this is pretty surprising behaviour, and that the *scratch* buffer should behave consistently by default. You might M-x report-emacs-bug. In some future version of Emacs (but hopefully not too soon) lexical-binding will become a default and this particular discrepancy would go away; but in the interim a suitable (even if slightly ugly) solution would be to add the comment to the default scratch message.

You can do this in your own config via C-hv initial-scratch-message.

Q: VScode, WSL, Ruby, Files Being Marked as Changed on Commit A:

I've faced this problem before. The common issue is due to

  • the OS Terminal detecting the file permissions

  • or the file line endings as file content changes

These are the common solutions (copied from gemini):

Exclude permissions from file content changes

Linux tracks whether a file is "executable," while Windows doesn't handle these bits the same way. Git often sees this as a change from 100644 to 100755.

To tell Git to ignore permission changes, run this command in your WSL terminal:

git config core.filemode false

Standardize Line Endings

Windows uses CRLF (\r\n), while Linux/WSL uses LF (\n). If your Windows Git client and WSL Git client aren't synced, every line looks "new" to the other system.

Run this in WSL to ensure Git converts files to LF on checkout and keeps them that way:

git config --global core.autocrlf input
